claim: Envoy AI Gateway/Agent Router is architected around an explicit 'Two-tier gateway pattern': a Tier One gateway for centralized auth, routing, and global token-based rate limiting across external AI providers, and a Tier Two gateway for fine-grained self-hosted model access with native InferencePool (endpoint picker) support.
stance_target: the layered pattern separating external-provider routing from self-hosted-pool routing is an intentional, named architectural tier in the reference implementation
scope_conditions: Envoy AI Gateway / Agent Router, project proposal dated Apr 24, 2026, approved
quoted_support: Tier One Gateway: Centralized entry point handling authentication, top-level routing, and global token-based rate limiting across all AI providers. Tier Two Gateway: Fine-grained control over self-hosted model access, with InferencePool (endpoint picker) support for LLM inference optimization.

stance_target: scope of the external-provider side of the layered pattern
scope_conditions: Envoy AI Gateway, as of April 2026
quoted_support: Unified API: Abstracts 16+ AI providers (OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, Google Gemini/Vertex AI, Anthropic, Mistral, Cohere, Groq, DeepSeek, and more) under a single OpenAI-compatible API.
